Subject: Order form redlines — indemnity carveout for model-derived output

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Attached is our v3 redline to the order form — we added language to carve out indemnity for third-party IP claims that are based solely on customer-provided content or customer-trainable workflows. We flagged two areas where we think Redwood's standard defend/reimburse language doesn't match our procurement policy: the carveout scope and the notice/cooperation timing.

Key asks from NovaPulse:
- Clarify that claims based solely on "customer input" or "customer-supplied fine-tuning data" are excluded from Redwood indemnity.
- Add a 30-day cure notice window before NovaPulse must substantively respond.
- Confirm that Redwood's obligations won't be triggered by downstream derivative output (i.e., model output that transforms customer prompts) unless Redwood incorporated third-party content into the model weights after contract signature.

We're happy to review proposed language. Attached: orderform_redline_v3.docx and an evidence_matrix.xlsx that shows sources NovaPulse is concerned about.

Can your legal team propose a narrow compromise? We want to avoid broad carveouts that create ops risk for Redwood but need protection for our training/data-workflows.

Best,
Claire

Subject: Re: Order form redlines — indemnity carveout for model-derived output

Claire — thanks for the redline and the matrix. We've reviewed at a high level and want to propose a path forward rather than a binary accept/reject. High-level thoughts:

1) We agree customer-provided training data should not force Redwood to defend unrelated third-party claims — reasonable to scope that out.
2) We are uncomfortable with a blanket exclusion for "derivative output" because that would let novel model outputs evade legitimate third-party claims (e.g., hallucinated verbatim copied text from a third party).
3) Notice/cure windows: we can consider a 30-day mutual review/cure step but need clarity on escalation and who controls litigation decisions.

Ben and Tessa from Legal/CS will draft compromise language and propose a short definition of "Customer Input" and a tightening of the derivative-output carveout to require demonstrable provenance (e.g., evidence the model response reproduces identifiable third-party material).

Propose we circulate a tracked-change snippet by end of day for your counsel to review. If that works, we can set a quick 30-minute sync tomorrow to nail the litigation control language.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference

Kimberly / Tessa — looping in my practical redlines. See inline suggestions below; I'll drop a tracked-change paragraph for the order form.

Inline notes:
- Define two terms: "Customer Content" (data, prompts, training corpora provided by customer) and "Customer-initiated Derivative" (model outputs that reproduce or are substantively traceable to Customer Content).
- Carveout proposal: exclude indemnity for claims solely arising from Customer Content. But if the claim arises because the model output reproduces third-party copyrighted material not supplied by the customer, Redwood retains defend obligations.
- Evidence burden: require NovaPulse to produce metadata/trace logs (we can accept summarized provenance) before the carveout applies. Put a 10-business-day window for evidence delivery.
- Litigation control: Redwood keeps primary defense but will consult and share material decisions; allow NovaPulse to participate at their expense.

Risks/ops: requiring heavy metadata could create friction; we should keep the evidence standard operationally feasible (hashes, timestamps, customer-supplied dataset manifest).

I will draft language that balances NovaPulse's ask and our operational constraints.

Ben
Sr. Commercial Counsel — Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Claire Huang <claire.huang@novapulse.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 13:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form redlines — indemnity carveout for model-derived output

Claire — attaching our proposed snippet (see below pasted) and a short operational checklist (we'll upload full tracked changes to the Drive link). Key points: preserve Redwood's defend obligation for third-party claims tied to model weights or to outputs that reproduce third-party material, but allow the carveout when: (i) the claim is demonstrably based only on Customer Content; and (ii) NovaPulse provides provenance within 10 business days.

Proposed snippet (for insertion into Order Form indemnity paragraph):
"Redwood's indemnity obligations shall not apply to claims to the extent they are based solely on Customer Content supplied to Redwood by Customer prior to the act alleged to give rise to the claim; provided, however, that Customer shall, within ten (10) business days of Redwood's written request, provide sufficient, good-faith provenance evidence (including dataset manifests, timestamps, and sample prompt/response logs) demonstrating that the allegedly infringing material originates in Customer Content. In the absence of such evidence, Redwood's indemnity obligations shall remain in effect for claims reasonably established to arise from Redwood's model weights or model outputs."

Operational checklist attached: evidence_matrix.xlsx — shows the minimum metadata fields we need.

If that language is acceptable in principle, can NovaPulse counsel confirm whether a 10-business-day evidence window and Redwood's retained defense control are acceptable? If not, propose changes.

Kimberly

Attachments referenced: orderform_snippet.txt (pasted above), evidence_matrix.xlsx (uploaded to Drive)

Kimberly / Claire — thanks for the exchange. From an external counsel perspective the proposed snippet is sensible as a middle ground. Two practical edits we recommend:

1) Replace "sufficient, good-faith provenance evidence" with a non-exhaustive list (dataset manifest, upload hashes, job IDs, relevant prompt/response excerpts) to avoid future disputes over what counts as "sufficient."
2) Add a mutual escalation step: if Redwood and NovaPulse disagree on provenance within the 10-business-day window, either party may trigger independent neutral technical review; the cost allocation should be split except where one party is shown to have acted unreasonably.

Proposed short edit (for insertion):
"...Customer shall, within ten (10) business days of Redwood's written request, provide provenance evidence such as dataset manifests, upload hashes, job identifiers, and representative prompt/response excerpts. If the parties cannot agree on the sufficiency of such evidence within that ten (10) business day period, either party may request an independent technical reviewer; the costs of such review shall be borne equally unless the reviewer finds one party's position to have been frivolous or unreasonable, in which case the reviewer shall allocate costs accordingly."

Happy to redline the Order Form directly in DocuSign if you prefer.

Regards,
